result.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts pretrained language models to unlabeled target-domain data using self-generated pseudo-labels, whose reliability remains poorly understood. We analyze majority-vote supervision for TTRL with online Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) and decompose its error into population-majority bias and prompt-dependent finite-rollout variation. Because population-majority bias is generally unidentifiable without external supervision, we focus on mitigating the downstream effects of finite-rollout variation. We propose \emph{Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO)}, which conditions within-prompt robust reweighting on observed vote reliability to make updates from sampling-sensitive prompts more conservative. We further introduce a cache-based mechanism to reduce self-supervised forgetting during online adaptation. Across six mathematical and knowledge-intensive reasoning benchmarks and five model backbones, PC-Dr.DPO matches or outperforms the strongest TTRL baseline in 24 of 30 settings.

AI.brief_summary: 该文分析测试时强化学习中多数投票伪标签的可靠性，将误差分解为总体多数偏差与有限采样波动，并提出按投票可靠性加权的鲁棒 DPO 及缓存机制以缓解在线适配中的遗忘。
AI.relevance_reason: 其基于投票可靠性的条件重加权与缓存式在线训练，可能为 LVR 中自生成推理轨迹的噪声监督筛选和更新稳定性提供可核查的方法线索，但未涉及视觉状态或 latent 推理。
